minutes.headline: Assessors heard a resident's warning that property card values don't match, then questioned the revaluation consultant on methods.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors met in person without Zoom. It heard a member's concern that property card values disagree, amended minutes for later review, and questioned the consultant on revaluation methods. It also discussed the website, an ad hoc citizen committee and an adjunct member, and moved to enter executive session not to return.

public_comment.topic: Resident on One Main Street urged keeping some gray area in roles between the board and town manager to build accountability.
Resident said the draft and final revaluation reports differ sharply and asked to see the math behind the ratios.
Suggested citizen volunteers could research what other towns do for land and building value policies.

what_happened.line: A board member raised that values on property cards do not match, and the chair and interim assessor will investigate and report on December 4.
The consultant answered the board's questions on revaluation methods, and said the existing general contract would cover the classification hearing work rather than a new RFP.
The November 6 minutes will be revised with members' amendments and reviewed at the next meeting; the October 11 minutes were deferred.
A resident said the draft and final revaluation reports differ sharply and asked to see the math behind the ratios.
The board moved to enter executive session; the minutes did not capture the roll call outcome. No votes were recorded.

why_it_matters: Property card values are the figures behind each home's assessment, so a mismatch between cards bears on how a tax bill is calculated and whether it can be trusted.
Residents asking to see the math behind the revaluation ratios points to the revaluation being checked in public before the classification hearing.
watch_next: December 4 meeting: the report on the property card discrepancies, review of the amended November 6 minutes, and the data collection manual draft as an agenda item.
